references.text: The same expression 'the Lord spoke to Moses' is repeated later in the same chapter, showing the continuous communication between God and Moses.
The Lord continues to speak to Moses and Aaron as a direct follow-up to the message that begins here.
The fixed formula 'the Lord spoke to Moses' is used repeatedly throughout Exodus to introduce divine instructions.
The same introductory formula 'the Lord spoke to Moses' opens Leviticus and shows how God communicates with His servant.
Numbers also begins with the Lord speaking to Moses, as a continuation of the same pattern for divine revelation.
The Lord's speech to Moses at the burning bush establishes the pattern for how God communicates directly with Moses.
